title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #2

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be? (1 mark)
   A. Below the jug
   B. At the same level as the water surface
   C. Above the jug
   D. Far from the jug

2. What is mulching? (1 mark)
   A. Digging deep holes
   B. Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   C. Removing all plants
   D. Burning grass

3. Which of these is a liquid used as fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Charcoal
   B. Firewood
   C. Air
   D. Paraffin

4. Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope? (1 mark)
   A. Magnetism only
   B. Sound
   C. Gravity
   D. Light

5. Why is a bucket better than a running tap for washing a bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the bicycle dirty
   B. It uses less water
   C. It makes it heavier
   D. It uses more water

6. What do fish use to take oxygen from water? (1 mark)
   A. Horns
   B. Feathers
   C. Lungs
   D. Gills

7. What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house? (1 mark)
   A. It blocks the sun completely
   B. It saves electricity in the day
   C. It uses more electricity
   D. It makes the house dark

8. An empty bottle is full of (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Nothing
   C. Air
   D. Water

9. Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are invisible
   B. They keep their shape and can support weight
   C. They flow easily
   D. They spread out

10. What is a compost pit used for? (1 mark)
   A. Burning waste
   B. Storing glass
   C. Storing plastic
   D. Turning kitchen waste into manure

11. What is the best way to deal with metal scrap in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   B. Throw it in a river
   C. Burn it
   D. Bury it in the school garden

12. Which of these is an example of reusing water? (1 mark)
   A. Buying bottled water
   B. Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   C. Pouring water down the drain
   D. Leaving taps open

13. A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Reproducing
   C. Responding to changes
   D. Growing

14. Why should electric irons be unplugged after use? (1 mark)
   A. To prevent burns and fire
   B. To make them noisy
   C. To make them hot
   D. To make them heavier

15. What does a red traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Speed up
   B. Stop
   C. Go
   D. Turn on lights

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure. (3 marks)

17. Convert 4 kg into grams. (2 marks)

18. Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line. (3 marks)

19. Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water. (4 marks)

20. Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — At the same level as the water surface
   This gives an accurate reading.

2. B — Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   Mulch reduces evaporation from the soil.

3. D — Paraffin
   Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

4. C — Gravity
   Gravity pulls water downhill.

5. B — It uses less water
   A bucket has a limited amount of water.

6. D — Gills
   Fish breathe using gills.

7. B — It saves electricity in the day
   Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

8. C — Air
   An empty bottle contains air.

9. B — They keep their shape and can support weight
   Solids keep their shape.

10. D — Turning kitchen waste into manure
   Decomposable waste rots into compost.

11. A — Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   Metal can be recycled.

12. B — Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   Using water twice is reusing.

13. C — Responding to changes
   The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

14. A — To prevent burns and fire
   Switching off prevents accidents.

15. B — Stop
   Red means stop.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4000 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
   Working / marking points: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.
